reviews.title: LÊ CÔNG MINH · IELTS 49 · W07 · Đề 1
reviews.overall: Em đã viết về đúng bảng và nhận ra Australia giảm, Thailand luôn đứng đầu. Tuy nhiên, em ghi 235,088 xe của Argentina thành số của Thailand; phần Overview chỉ nói Thailand tăng mà bỏ qua việc sản lượng giảm sau đỉnh năm 2006. Bài mới có 140 từ, dưới mức 150 từ, và nhiều câu thiếu động từ chính hoặc ghép các mệnh đề bằng dấu phẩy. Bài này em soát chưa kỹ. Cô yêu cầu em đối chiếu lại từng số với nước và năm, viết đủ hai câu hoàn chỉnh cho mỗi Detail, rồi kiểm tra lại ngữ pháp và độ dài trước khi nộp.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em đã tách Introduction, Overview và hai đoạn Detail, nhưng Detail 1 trộn diễn biến của Thailand với Australia, còn Detail 2 lặp Thailand và gần như không đưa số liệu của Argentina. Mốc 2006 là điểm Thailand đạt đỉnh và Argentina vượt Australia; em có thể chia Detail theo giai đoạn 2003–2006 rồi 2006–2009 để các so sánh rõ hơn. Mỗi Detail cần ít nhất hai câu hoàn chỉnh.

The two line charts compare the numbers of male and female prisoners in a European country from 1911 to 2001.

Overall, the male prison population remained larger than the female population throughout the period. Male numbers fell early on but rose markedly towards the end, whereas female numbers declined overall despite several later fluctuations.

In 1911 and 1921, there were about 18,000 male prisoners. The figure dropped to roughly 10,000 in 1931 and stayed close to that level in 1941. It then recovered to around 19,000 in 1951 and remained near 20,000 until 1971. From there, it jumped to approximately 39,000 in 1981 before reaching a peak of about 46,000 in 2001.

By contrast, the number of female prisoners started at about 3,200 in 1911 and fell steadily to a low of roughly 500 in 1941. It subsequently rose to around 1,500 in 1961, dipped to about 700 in 1971, and then increased gradually. By 2001, the figure stood at approximately 1,900, still below its initial level.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line chart shows how much fish and four types of meat were eaten in a European country from 1979 to 2004.
Overall, there was a general increase in chicken consumption, with this food item experiencing the most pronounced rise, while an opposite trend was observed in the figures for beef and lamb. Also of note is that beef consistently had the highest figures throughout the majority of the years.
To elaborate, about 220 grams of beef was eaten in 1979, with a subsequent peak of 240 grams in 1984 and a final decrease to about 130 grams in 2004. The figures for chicken, by contrast, started lower at 140 grams but grew steadily to hit a peak of 250 grams at the end of the period.
Regarding categories with lower figures, lamb consumption started at 150 grams, after which it experienced a decline to 100 grams in 1994, before ending the period at 60 grams. A similar pattern was, however, recorded in the figures for fish, which began at 60 grams and finished at nearly 50 grams.

Overall, chicken consumption rose substantially and became the highest by the end of the period, overtaking beef in the late 1980s. By contrast, beef and lamb fell markedly, whereas fish declined only slightly and remained the least consumed food throughout.

The line graph compares the percentage of women who were members of parliament in five countries in Europe between 2000 and 2012.
Overall, it is clear that the percentage of female parliament members in most countries increased over the period. Germany had the highest percentage for most of the time, while the UK always had the lowest percentage.

France also grew steadily to reach approximately 28% in 2012.
Looking at the other countries, Belgium began at about 17% in 2000. It increased quickly to around 28% in 2004 and then stayed around this level until 2012. Finally, the UK had the lowest percentage in 2000, at only about 3%. Although it increased to around 27% in 2012, it was still lower than the other nations.

reviews.originalEssay:
The pie charts show the main reasons why students selected a specific university in the United Kingdom in two different years, 1997 and 2007.
Overall, it is clear that the most popular reason for choosing a university in both years was suitable degree courses. In contrast, the quality of resources was the least important factor for students in both 1997 and 2007.
In 1997, the percentage of students choosing a university because of suitable degree courses was the highest, at 35%. This figure increased slightly to 37% in 2007. The second biggest reason in 1997 was the quality of teaching at 21%, but this fell to 17% after ten years. Similarly, the proportion of students who cared about the quality of resources also went down from 19% in 1997 to 16% in 2007.
Looking at the other reasons, proximity to parental home was chosen by 15% of students in 1997, and this number grew significantly to 22% in 2007. Finally, good sports and social activities was the least popular reason in 1997 at only 10%. However, it decreased even further to just 6% in 2007.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The pie charts illustrate how the proportions of students citing five reasons for choosing a particular university in the United Kingdom changed between 1997 and 2007.

Overall, the percentages citing suitable courses, proximity to parental home and teaching quality rose, whereas those for resources and sports and social activities declined. Suitable courses remained the leading reason in both years; proximity to parental home was the least cited in 1997, while sports and social activities ranked last in 2007.

In 1997, 35% of students chose the university because it offered suitable degree courses, with this figure edging up to 37% in 2007. The proportion citing teaching quality also rose, from 15% to 18%. By contrast, the share selecting the institution for its resources fell from 21% to 17%, although resources were the second most common reason in 1997.

Among the other reasons, proximity to parental home accounted for 10% in 1997 and 22% in 2007, the largest increase at 12 percentage points. Sports and social activities followed the opposite pattern: their share fell from 19% to just 6%, a drop of 13 percentage points, the greatest decline among the five reasons.
